baseline.event_date_basis: converted from the vendor's UTC instant to Sydney time

options.reason: No ASX single-stock option chain is retrievable free from this container. Measured 2026-09-22 on the repo's own authenticated Yahoo path: AAPL 22 expiries, BHP.AX and CBA.AX zero. So there is no event-implied move and no 25-delta skew, and `positioning` below carries the substitute. This stage runs in the regime archive/backtest/FINDINGS.md section 33 priced at rho=+0.073, p=0.45 over 104 events.

consensus.caveat: Australian sell-side coverage is thin below the ASX 200 and an empty list is common. It is not a signal.

history.caveat: Dates and timestamps are the ASX's own announcement record, so these are real prints and may be cited as facts about a date -- unlike researcher_japan, whose history is a cadence estimate. What is still inferred is the CLASSIFIER: a results release whose headline carries no results vocabulary is missed, which is the Trustpilot failure mode stage EU measured. A year in years_that_returned_nothing was not read, not a quiet year. `filer_type` of quarterly_report_only means this issuer lodges an Appendix 4C or 5B rather than a 4D or 4E -- a cash-flow statement, not a profit result -- which is a di…

positioning.basis: ASIC's aggregated daily short position report. NOT a 0.5% disclosure register: every product with a reported position appears, and 430 of 755 rows on 2026-09-16 were below 0.5%. An absent product therefore has no reported short position at all, which is a measured zero rather than a truncation. The file is published about four business days in arrears -- see lag_sessions.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of OBSERVED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it says nothing about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Unlike stage J's, the history half rests on real announcement dates.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read au_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR carried over from stage J, none is measured on Australian data, and au_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters today is only that this is not identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival rather than the same number wearing two hats.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus an OBSERVED reaction history, capped because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved off ASIC's untruncated daily register, capped because neither is skew. The register is 4 sessions stale and that is not discounted here -- read it off positioning.lag_sessions.

first_hunter_context.bar: There is no sourced street EPS line. Morgans (downgrade to Hold, target $6.40, week of 6 Oct 2026) expects 'a mid-single digit decline in 2H26 earnings (ex notable costs)' on 1H cash NPAT of $176m, i.e. roughly $165-170m in 2H. Consensus FY26 EPS is about 47.7-49c (FNArena; Yahoo shows 0.49 across 12 analysts, revised down from 0.53 over 90 days). The 14-analyst target is $6.27-6.29, below the $6.49 spot. The company's own bar (1H26 outlook): 'tailwinds to margin', sub-inflation FY26 cost growth, home lending contraction easing, growth in FY27. Sources: https://www.ibtimes.com.au/boq-shares-rise-ahead-full-year-results-1876599 , https://www.fnarena.com/index.php/analysis-data/consensus-forecasts/stock-analysis/?code=BOQ , https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260422/pdf/06yqn40qfhs68p.pdf. Two partly agreeing estimate sources plus a company statement, so sizes are not capped, but the bar is loose.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: ASIC aggregate short 4.49% (29.6m shares) as of 2026-10-08, up from 4.23% on 10-01 (+0.26pp, building), lag 4 sessions. This is elevated for an ASX bank, and sentiment is bearish (1 Buy / 7 Hold / 6 Sell, average target below spot), so the bar is low and a crowded short is fuel against a negative. The baseline lean already carries this at +2.2. Over the lag the stock went 6.38 -> 6.69 -> 6.49; it fell 3.0% on 14 Oct with the sector (BEN -3.5%, CBA -2.2%), so nothing idiosyncratic happened into the seal. I did not size positioning as a separate finding, because it would only restate the baseline lean.
first_hunter_context.session_check: bmo. The webcast notice puts the briefing at 10:00 AEDT on the day, the open. All five prior results in the ASX record were lodged 08:15-08:43 Sydney (e.g. 22/04/2026 08:15 and 08:32). https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20261006/pdf/074zbk1qbc4rz0.pdf

evidence.text: APRA's monthly ADI statistics show BOQ's resident housing loans fell from $52,790m (Feb 2026) to $50,731m (Aug 2026), -$2,059m or -3.9% over 2H26. That is the same pace as 1H26 (-$2,095m from Aug 2025), against the 1H26 guide that 'home lending contraction [is] easing'. Total resident deposits fell 3.1% ($68,791m to $66,648m). Two caveats: Jul-Aug flattened (Aug -$2m), and business loans rose to $15,827m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 1H26 (22 Apr 2026): retail GLA fell $1.5bn and NIM fell 3bp; the stock moved -9.08%, the worst of five observed prints. FY25 (15 Oct 2025): +1.40%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The series is public and analysts who track it would have it in the mid-single-digit 2H decline estimates. What may not be priced is the read-through to the FY27 'return to home lending growth' guide: if the market had absorbed it, consensus FY27 numbers would have been cut alongside the downgrades, and the 90-day revision visible on Yahoo (0.53 to 0.49) is roughly the size of the $33m notable item alone.
evidence.independence: The company's own 1H26 deck says home lending contraction was easing (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260422/pdf/06yqnk5f5h2d6l.pdf). It cuts the other way and is not corroboration. Otherwise none.

evidence.text: Rising cash rates point to a 2H26 margin lift. BOQ's 1H26 deck lists '2H26 considerations: benefits from an increasing cash rate environment, replicating portfolio and hedging benefits, ... tailwinds from TD spreads, deposit pricing and funding mix'. Peer Bendigo & Adelaide reported a 2H26 NIM of 1.98%, up 6bp half on half, on deposit mix, TD repricing and the replicating portfolio (results 18 Aug 2026).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM -3bp at 1H26 -> -9.08%. NIM +10bp y/y at FY25 (1.67% vs 1.57% the half before) -> +1.40%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company guided it and BEN printed it two months ago. If the margin lift were fully in numbers, Morgans would not still be forecasting a mid-single-digit 2H decline. It is consistent with that forecast only if volume loss (finding 1) offsets the margin gain, so the two findings net against each other and are not double-counted.
evidence.independence: Bendigo FY26: https://www.businessnewsaustralia.com/articles/bendigo-bank-lifts-full-year-profit-to-530m-as-lower-cost-deposit-growth-buoys-margins.html (a different issuer, but the same proxy mechanism)

evidence.text: Capital is still in surplus and the buyback is mostly unspent. BOQ's 10 Aug release gives a pro-forma CET1 of 11.01% after the $295m return, against a 10.25-10.75% target range. The 1 Sep Appendix 3C shows only about 1.72m shares (about $11.1m) of the $196m on-market buyback bought before the results blackout. So about $185m resumes after the print, and the surplus above the range invites an upsize or a final-dividend payout at the top of 60-75%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The capital return announcement on 10 Aug 2026 is not in the results history and I did not measure its reaction. No observed result in the history carried a capital-return surprise.
evidence.why_not_priced: The buyback and the CET1 are public. What is not priced is any upsize from the remaining 26-76bp above the top of the range. If the market expected one, the sell-side would not sit at 6 Sell with targets below spot. Resumed buying of about $0.7m a day against $9.6m median turnover is real but small support.
evidence.independence: Appendix 3C buyback update, 1 Sep 2026: https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260901/pdf/073kc2jc49qgsd.pdf (the same issuer, a different document)

evidence.text: The 2H26 notable items and the cost outcome were pre-released on 10 Aug 2026: a $47m pre-tax ($33m post-tax) technology and asset impairment, excluded from the final dividend base, and 'Excluding this notable item, BOQ is on track to meet guidance of sub-inflation expense growth for FY26'. That removes most of the kitchen-sink and cost-miss risk at the first full-year result under CEO Rod Finch.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: At 1H26, a $31m post-tax held-for-sale loss sat in statutory profit and the stock fell -9.08%, though cash earnings and NIM were the drivers.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is priced: it was disclosed two months ago and consensus EPS fell by roughly that amount over 90 days. I filed it at zero because it lands inside what the company already said. Its value is that it narrows the downside tail, not that it gives a direction.
evidence.independence: Yahoo consensus FY26 EPS revision from 0.53 to 0.49 over 90 days, cited in the IBTimes and ad-hoc-news coverage: https://www.ibtimes.com.au/boq-shares-rise-ahead-full-year-results-1876599

evidence.text: The 1H26 deck warns that 'there may be further statutory impacts recognised in 2H26, upon completion' of the Challenger whole-of-loan sale, which completed 1 May 2026. The 10 Aug release did not quantify any such item, so a further statutory loss is possible.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the same held-for-sale line as at 1H26 ($31m post-tax loss, -9.08% day, with other drivers).
evidence.why_not_priced: It sits below cash earnings, has no path to the guide and is flagged as non-cash, so I sized it at a fraction.
